description: Observation stations used to verify forecasts. Positions and depths come from the providers' own data (see position_source). paired_spots distances are great-circle km from the station to the break (distance_km) and to the spot's offshore forecast point (forecast_point_distance_km). See docs/observations.md.

paired_spots.note: Open-shelf buoy in 60 m ESE of Point Danger; samples the E-SE trade swell and S-SE groundswell before it wraps into the Gold Coast points. The breaks sit behind headlands, so southerly swell is refracted and reduced there, and the point setups respond to direction very differently from the open buoy. Realtime only (not QC'd) and H1/3 rather than spectral Hs.

paired_spots.note: About 25 km SSE of Trestles off the north San Diego County coast, inside the Southern California Bight: like Trestles it is partly shadowed from W-NW swell by the Channel Islands and open to S-SW swell, so it is the closest comparable exposure. The cobblestone points at Trestles refract and focus swell, and island shadowing changes over short distances with direction, so buoy Hs is an offshore reference, not surf height. Position is the GFS-Wave output point until NDBC metadata replaces it.
